Q0134

“The Master said: Is it not a pleasure to learn and to…” — Confucius (Q0134)

An English quotation associated with Analects, Xue Er, organized here under learning.

Quotes / Confucius / Q0134

English

The Master said: Is it not a pleasure to learn and to practice what one has learned in due time? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to remain unresentful when others fail to appreciate one?
Thinker Confucius
School Confucianism
Source Analects, Xue Er
Theme Learning
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Analects, Xue Er, within the Confucianism tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of learning, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Confucius's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
